title: FastAPI from Scratch
moduleObjectives: Create and activate a Python virtual environment with `python3 -m venv` and pin project dependencies in a `requirements.txt`
Build FastAPI routes (GET, POST, DELETE) that use typed path parameters, query parameters, and JSON request bodies
Validate request data with Pydantic models and interpret FastAPI's automatic 422 validation errors
Organize a growing application into per-resource routers using `APIRouter` prefixes and tags
Implement shared logic such as header-based authentication and database sessions with `Depends` dependency injection
Containerize the app with a Dockerfile and run it alongside Postgres using Docker Compose with healthchecks and named volumes
Persist data to Postgres using SQLAlchemy ORM models, an engine, and per-request sessions
Return correct HTTP status codes with `HTTPException` and verify every endpoint with both `curl` and the `/docs` Swagger UI

lessons.title: Prerequisites Check
lessons.objective: Verify that Python 3, pip, Docker (without sudo), Docker Compose, curl, and the course directory from Modules 01 and 02 all still work before starting FastAPI.

lessons.title: Python Virtual Environment
lessons.objective: Create, activate, and deactivate a project-scoped virtual environment with `python3 -m venv` and explain when to use a venv on the host versus running in Docker.

lessons.title: Installing FastAPI
lessons.objective: Install FastAPI and Uvicorn into the active venv and freeze the exact package versions into a `requirements.txt` with `pip freeze`.

lessons.title: Hello World
lessons.objective: Write a minimal FastAPI app in `main.py`, run it with `uvicorn main:app --reload`, and verify responses from curl, a browser, and the `/docs` Swagger UI.

lessons.title: Path and Query Params
lessons.objective: Define routes with typed path parameters and optional query parameters, and demonstrate FastAPI rejecting mistyped input with 422 validation errors.

lessons.title: Request Bodies with Pydantic
lessons.objective: Validate JSON request bodies on a `POST /items` route with a Pydantic `BaseModel` and test valid and invalid payloads from both curl and Swagger UI.

lessons.title: Multiple Routes and Routers
lessons.objective: Refactor routes into per-resource modules using `APIRouter` with prefixes and tags, and mount them in `main.py` with `app.include_router`.

lessons.title: Dependencies and Injection
lessons.objective: Implement a header-checking `get_current_user` dependency with `Depends` and apply it at route level and router level, distinguishing 401 and 422 responses.

lessons.title: Containerizing FastAPI
lessons.objective: Write a Dockerfile that caches the pip-install layer, build the image, and run the containerized app with uvicorn bound to `0.0.0.0` so the mapped port is reachable.

lessons.title: Docker Compose and Postgres
lessons.objective: Orchestrate the FastAPI app and a Postgres database with `docker-compose.yml`, using a healthcheck, a named volume, a bind-mounted hot-reload dev loop, and a `.env` file for secrets.

lessons.title: Database with SQLAlchemy
lessons.objective: Replace the in-memory item store with Postgres persistence using a SQLAlchemy engine, ORM models, and a `get_db` session dependency, then verify the rows directly in psql.

lessons.title: Error Handling and Status Codes
lessons.objective: Return correct HTTP status codes (201, 204, 400, 404) by setting `status_code` on route decorators and raising `HTTPException` for missing resources and business-rule violations.

lessons.title: Final Checkpoint
lessons.objective: Build a complete `Profile` resource from memory — SQLAlchemy model, router, protected DELETE, and correct status codes — and pass a 10-step curl acceptance test.

quiz.question: You run `python -c "import main"` and get `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastapi'`. According to the lessons, what is the most likely cause?
options: FastAPI must be reinstalled with `sudo pip install fastapi`
The virtual environment is not activated in this terminal — `(.venv)` is missing from the prompt
`main.py` is missing the `app = FastAPI()` line
Uvicorn is not running yet
quiz.feedback: The lessons call a forgotten `source .venv/bin/activate` the number-one mistake of the module, and this error is its telltale symptom.

quiz.question: In the command `uvicorn main:app --reload`, what do `main` and `app` refer to?
options: `main` is the project directory and `app` is the Dockerfile stage to run
`main` is the entry function and `app` is the value it returns
`main` is the Python file (without `.py`) and `app` is the FastAPI instance variable inside it
`main` is the git branch and `app` is the name given to the process
quiz.feedback: The lesson explains that `main` names the module file and `app` names the FastAPI object, so renaming the file to `app.py` would change the command to `uvicorn app:app --reload`.

quiz.question: A route is declared as `def read_item(item_id: int)`. What happens when a client requests `/items/banana`?
options: 200 OK with `{"item_id": "banana"}` returned as a string
404 Not Found because the path does not match any route
500 Internal Server Error from the failed type conversion
422 Unprocessable Entity with a validation error naming the failing field
quiz.feedback: FastAPI reads the `int` type hint and automatically rejects non-integer input with a 422 whose body says which field failed and why.

quiz.question: A curl POST to `/items` with a correct-looking JSON payload keeps failing with a `json_invalid` error. Per the lesson, what is the most common cause?
options: The `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` header is missing from the request
The URL was not quoted, so the shell consumed the `?` character
The `-X POST` flag must come after the `-d` flag
Uvicorn must be restarted after every POST request
quiz.feedback: The lesson demonstrates that omitting the `Content-Type: application/json` header prevents FastAPI from parsing the body and calls it the top cause of unexplained errors on POST.

quiz.question: A router is created with `APIRouter(prefix="/items", tags=["items"])`. How should you declare the route that lists items at the path `/items`?
options: `@app.get("/items")` inside the router file
`@router.get("/items")`
`@router.get("")`
`@router.get("/list")`
quiz.feedback: The prefix is already applied by the router, so `@router.get("")` maps to `/items`, while `@router.get("/items")` would wrongly produce `/items/items`.

quiz.question: The `get_current_user` dependency requires an `X-Token` header. What does the protected route return when the header is present but has the wrong value?
options: 422, because the header failed Pydantic validation
401, because the dependency raises `HTTPException(status_code=401)` for an invalid token
403, because the user lacks permission for the resource
404, because protected routes are hidden without authentication
quiz.feedback: The lesson distinguishes 422 (header missing, rejected by framework-level validation) from 401 (header present but wrong, raised by the dependency's `HTTPException`).

quiz.question: Why must the Dockerfile's `CMD` run uvicorn with `--host 0.0.0.0`?
options: It enables hot-reload inside the container
It tells Docker which port to publish on the host
It runs uvicorn with elevated privileges so it can open port 8000
It makes uvicorn listen beyond the container's loopback so `docker run -p` traffic from the host can reach it
quiz.feedback: The lesson calls this the most common Dockerfile mistake: without `--host 0.0.0.0`, uvicorn binds only to the container's loopback and curl from the host gets a connection reset despite the port mapping.

quiz.question: In the Compose stack, what hostname should the FastAPI container use in its connection string to reach Postgres?
options: `db`, the service name defined in `docker-compose.yml`
`localhost`, since both containers run on the same machine
`postgres`, the name of the Docker image
`127.0.0.1:5432`, the port mapped to the host
quiz.feedback: Inside the Compose network, containers reach each other by service name, so the connection string is `postgresql://postgres:devpass@db:5432/appdb` — typing `localhost` is called the number-one connection-string mistake.

quiz.question: In the SQLAlchemy create pattern `db.add(db_item)`, `db.commit()`, `db.refresh(db_item)`, what does the `db.refresh` call do?
options: It re-runs the pending SQL statements in case the commit failed
It clears the session cache so the next request starts clean
It reloads database-generated values like the auto-increment `id` back onto the object
It creates the table if it does not exist yet
quiz.feedback: The lesson warns that skipping `db.refresh(db_item)` leaves the response with `id: null` because the auto-generated id is only loaded back from the database by the refresh.

quiz.question: The lesson adds a check that rejects items with `price <= 0` using a 400 response. Why 400 rather than 422?
options: 400 signals a violation of your own business rules, while FastAPI reserves 422 for Pydantic's structural validation errors
422 is deprecated in FastAPI and 400 is its replacement
400 makes FastAPI automatically roll back the database transaction
422 responses cannot include a custom `detail` message
quiz.feedback: The lesson states that validation errors are always 422 (raised automatically by Pydantic), while 400 Bad Request is for business-rule violations you enforce in your own route code.
